macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks mostly higher as earnings offset AI and rate concerns
items.summary: The Dow rose 1.02% to 52,495.88 and the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,712.57, while the Nasdaq slipped 0.02% to 26,424.82. Small-cap stocks outperformed, with the Russell 2000 up 1.65%, as investors weighed strong earnings against elevated Treasury yields and oil prices.

items.title: SpaceX and Super Micro boost technology shares before the open
items.summary: U.S. futures pointed higher after SpaceX rose about 9% premarket following its first profit as a public company and Super Micro Computer surged nearly 13% on an upbeat outlook. Netflix fell more than 6% after lowering advertising-sales guidance.

items.title: Oil remains above $110 as Middle East risks support energy prices
items.summary: Brent crude traded near or above $110 a barrel amid heightened concerns surrounding the Iran conflict, Gulf shipping and attacks on regional infrastructure. Higher energy prices continue to complicate the inflation and interest-rate outlook.

items.title: Fed rate outlook remains focused on inflation risks
items.summary: Markets largely expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates at its October 28 meeting, while futures implied an 83% probability of no change. Policymakers remain divided, with inflation pressures and rising energy costs reducing expectations for near-term rate cuts.

items.title: Treasury yields stay elevated as 10-year rate tops 5.1%
items.summary: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was around 5.13%, keeping pressure on equity valuations and mortgage-sensitive sectors. Weaker housing data offered some relief to yields, but investors continued to assess the implications of persistent inflation and restrictive monetary policy.

items.title: Tesla, Meta and IBM earnings set to dominate the next session
items.summary: Investors are awaiting quarterly results from Tesla, Meta Platforms and IBM, with attention centered on AI returns, data-center spending and companies’ 2027 capital-expenditure plans. Netflix’s weaker advertising outlook has heightened scrutiny of technology-sector guidance.

items.title: General Motors falls after outlook disappoints
items.summary: General Motors shares dropped 6.8% despite third-quarter revenue rising 2.9% year over year to $50.02 billion, as its guidance fell short of analyst expectations. GE Aerospace also declined despite strong results and higher 2026 guidance.

items.title: Hasbro jumps on strong quarterly results
items.summary: Hasbro gained 11% after reporting stronger third-quarter results, supported by growth in its digital-gaming business. Equifax and other companies also contributed to the broader earnings-driven advance in U.S. equities.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades in a volatile $80,000–$83,000 range
items.summary: Bitcoin moved sharply during the past 24 hours, with reports ranging from a rebound above $83,000 to a decline below $80,000. Derivatives liquidations exceeded $90 million in one hour, while reported U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows showed a net outflow of 3,209 BTC.

items.title: Solana launches Alpenglow network upgrade
items.summary: Solana’s Alpenglow, described as its largest network overhaul since 2020, went live with a new voting system and a target of roughly 150-millisecond transaction finality.

items.title: Russia moves to restrict direct peer-to-peer crypto transfers
items.summary: Updated Bank of Russia guidance says direct individual-to-individual crypto transactions will need to move through authorized intermediaries after July 1, 2027. The guidance also prohibits transfers from digital accounts to self-custodial wallets.

items.title: Polygon releases security update for Bor
items.summary: Polygon Labs released Bor v2.10.3 to fix two medium-severity denial-of-service vulnerabilities affecting parallel block execution in BlockSTM V2. The vulnerabilities were reported through the Immunefi bug bounty program.

items.title: Ripple supports SEC crypto-market framework
items.summary: Ripple backed the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets plan and called for a clearer U.S. regulatory framework for digital assets.

items.title: Switzerland approves first retail spot Bitcoin fund
items.summary: FINMA approved Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund available to retail investors, reportedly granting an exemption from statutory diversification requirements.

items.title: Sui expands cross-chain USDC transfers with CCTP V2
items.summary: Sui announced that Circle’s Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol V2 is live on the network, enabling native USDC transfers between Sui and 29 other supported blockchains without conventional bridges.

items.title: France advances proposed tax on crypto-to-stablecoin swaps
items.summary: France’s National Assembly approved an amendment that would impose a roughly 31% capital-gains tax on crypto-to-stablecoin transactions, potentially ending tax deferrals for those trades from January 2027 if enacted.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA Sports revives Fight Night boxing franchise
items.summary: EA Sports announced the return of its Fight Night series, ending a 15-year hiatus. The publisher has not yet revealed the official title, release date, developer, or platforms.[2][6]

items.title: Crimson Desert DLC adds marriage, castles, and businesses
items.summary: Crimson Desert’s Charting the Unknown DLC is scheduled to launch October 29 and will add expanded relationship and kingdom-management features, including marriage, castle ownership, and businesses.[1]

items.title: Next Xbox reportedly could cost up to $1,800
items.summary: Reports claim Microsoft’s next Xbox console could launch in 2028 at a price as high as $1,800. The reports come as Xbox continues planned cuts affecting thousands of developers.[1][7]

items.title: Evil Geniuses reportedly set to shut down
items.summary: Esports organization Evil Geniuses is reported to be closing on November 2, 2026, ending a 27-year presence in competitive gaming.[8]

items.title: Multiple October game releases and platform expansions announced
items.summary: Games including Zero Parades: Director’s Cut, Mouthwashing, Shrek 2 Remastered, Faraway, and Ordinary Oddness announced release dates or expansions to additional platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch, and PC.[1]

items.title: Shrek 2 Remastered scheduled ahead of GTA VI
items.summary: DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered was officially announced after appearing on the Xbox Store, with a reported November 10 release date—nine days before Grand Theft Auto VI.[10]

items.title: Industry leaders debate smaller game development and AI use
items.summary: Recent industry coverage highlights pressure to reduce the scale and cost of blockbuster development, while reports indicate widespread AI adoption among studio leaders and continued debate over human-led game art.[3][5]
